findings: I found no blocking security risks. The change adds a test-only file reader, fixtures and one JSON evidence file. It touches no src/, brand/, design/, brain/ or .github/ paths, and nothing deploys.

runDirectoryProblems in tests/design-v4-square-product.test.js reads only the fixed names reviewer-design.output.md and owner-acceptance.json under a directory URL the test supplies. No external or user-controlled input reaches the path, so there is no traversal risk. It runs no eval or shell, and JSON.parse sits in a try/catch. A missing or malformed record falls back to the unfiltered problem list, so it fails closed. F5-invalid-not-json covers this.

The record validation is strict: accepted must be exactly true, and accepted_by, date, act and a citation must all be non-empty strings. For a deploy the citation must be production_version plus source_commit. The gate_record alternative applies only when act does not mention 'deploy'. A deploy act therefore cannot be accepted on a bare gate_record. F5 covers the false and missing-citation cases.

Rule A is scoped narrowly. Acceptance clears only 'has an uncleared gap', 'not cleared' for an image that has that gap, and ' / fails'. Absence problems ('not addressed', 'no design/reference/ reference', unmentioned axis) are never filtered. F3 and F4-axis-unmentioned-accepted assert this, so a forged record cannot hide missing coverage.

Residual risk, inherent to the design and not a defect: owner-acceptance.json is self-attested. It is not signed, and the test does not check production_version or source_commit against any deploy system. Anyone who can commit to runs/ can add a record that clears a recorded gap or axis failure for that run. Review of the evidence directory and the human gate remain the control, and this is within the owner's stated decision.

Rule B treats 'not applicable' as cleared only when the clause is not also a failure. F4-not-applicable-but-failed asserts that a recorded failure still surfaces, so the change adds no path where 'not applicable' hides a failure. Minor: the check is the loose regex /\bnot applicable\b/ and is clause-scoped. It could mark a wrongly phrased clause as cleared, but this is bounded to the same image and axis and does not weaken anything the spec requires.

The real record runs/wo-gh-8/owner-acceptance.json is a new untracked file with no secrets, tokens or credentials. It holds the 8-hex production version and the public commit SHA. A grep over tests/fixtures and that file for token, secret, key or password found nothing. git shows no modification to runs/wo-gh-8/reviewer-design.output.md. Only the new addendum file is added there.
